ns2:section.sectionText: This course will cover the gendered dimensions of security as they relate to war and political violence. We will address debates drawn from the recent research on gender and conflict. We will explore feminist approaches to international security and critically engage concepts like nationalism, peacekeeping, and militarism. We will explore the roles and strategies of women as agents of peace and violence during and after conflict. We will discuss the entrenched constructions such as “peaceful women,” “warrior men.” Topics that we will cover include feminist approaches to security, gendered dimensions of nationalism, the relationship between gender equality and international security, violence against women and men during peace and conflict times, women’s involvement in violent political organizations, conflict-related sexual violence, and women’s role during and after the conflict. This course will enhance students’ understanding on the gendered dimensions of security as a system of social constructs that creates social hierarchies and different forms of insecurities.
